chief_complaint: Uncontrolled blood sugar and increased thirst
transcript:
Doctor: Mr. Okafor, your glucose was 310 on the finger stick today. How have you been feeling?
Patient: Very tired all the time, drinking a lot of water, and going to the bathroom constantly. I've also lost about 12 pounds over the last month without trying.
Doctor: Any blurred vision or tingling in your feet?
Patient: Yes, my feet have been tingling and sometimes numb, especially at night.
Doctor: Do you have any family history of diabetes?
Patient: My mother had type 2 diabetes.
Doctor: What are you eating typically?
Patient: Mostly fast food, I work long hours. I haven't been exercising.
Doctor: On exam your BMI is 34, blood pressure 142 over 88. I can see early background retinopathy on fundoscopic exam. Monofilament test shows decreased sensation in both feet up to the ankle — that's diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Your hemoglobin A1c came back at 10.2 percent. This confirms type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient: What do I need to do?
Doctor: I'm starting you on metformin 500mg twice daily with meals to minimize GI side effects, and we'll titrate up to 1000mg twice daily after two weeks if tolerated. Given your A1c and symptoms, I'm also starting glipizide 5mg daily with breakfast. We need to refer you to ophthalmology for the retinopathy and get a urine microalbumin to check for kidney involvement. I'm also referring you to a diabetes educator and dietitian.
Patient: Will I need insulin?
Doctor: Not yet. We'll reassess at your three-month follow-up. Monitor your glucose before meals and at bedtime. Target fasting glucose is 80 to 130. Also need to check your feet daily.
Patient: Okay. And the tingling — will that get better?
Doctor: Improved glucose control usually slows progression. I'll prescribe gabapentin 300mg at bedtime for the neuropathic pain if it's bothering you.
Patient: Yes please, it keeps me up at night.
